source.title: A Black Box Made Less Opaque (part 2)

record.tranche_reason: Measures SAE-feature specialization and activation-space similarity in GPT-2 Small, providing a conceptual test of indirect evidence for recoverable features in an LLM, but not reproducing the original toy-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own measurements of SAE specialist features and full SAE activation vectors. The earlier Phase 1 findings it references are not treated as results here. The math-completion accuracy analysis is not a result for any listed claim version. Figure-specific values not stated in the text are not inferred.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained SAEs on GPT-2 Small as a tool to ask whether top features track syntax or meaning. It reports no sparsity, reconstruction, neuron-spread or superposition measurement, so its results do not bear on whether superposition or recoverable sparse features exist (V4). It also does not test completeness, stability or canonicity (V5), dimensionality (V6), or causes of polysemanticity (V2/V3). It assumes SAE features are meaningful units.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author concludes that top specialist SAE features respond mainly to syntax, while the full SAE representation clusters by topic, and suggests an unproven two-tier structure. The behavioural link is inconclusive because GPT-2 Small cannot do the math completions. Confidence in generalizing to modern models is low.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained residual-stream SAEs, matched text pairs, specialist-feature overlap and full-vector cosine/PCA analysis in GPT-2 Small; it does not use the original toy-network setup or test capacity-driven superposition.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported analyses focus on layer 11; the author states that specialization emerges in earlier layers for more symbolically laden forms. Topic and surface form also change specialist activation and overlap.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small layer-11 residual SAEs, top specialist features differ across surface forms of the same concept (mean Jaccard 0.13). Full SAE activation vectors cluster by topic (cosine 0.50 same-topic vs 0.14 cross-topic).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Highly active SAE features track surface syntax, while the aggregate SAE representation tracks topic or semantics (a proposed two-tier structure).

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: Evidence is limited to GPT-2 Small and the author notes low confidence in application to modern models. The PCA projection shows approximately 13% of the geometry. Several figure results are described qualitatively without their values in the text; the specialist-score threshold of 5.0 is described as somewhat arbitrary. The author says the math-completion analysis is inconclusive because the model had near-zero ability on the task.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version result rows left out. The math-completion examples and accuracy result are omitted because they do not measure a behavior named by the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy models, feature/dimension ratio, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Does not measure neuron-level spread, SAE sparsity or reconstruction, or whether the model contains recoverable sparse features; it presupposes the SAE.
No completeness, stability, or cross-SAE canonicity tests.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is unfounded: the study takes SAE recoverability for granted and never measures superposition, sparsity or neuron spread. Its results concern what SAE features encode (syntax vs semantics). A blog-style LessWrong replication exercise with no controls beyond cross-topic comparison; uncertainty is reported only as 'statistically significant'.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, feature count relative to dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, overlap geometry, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE-derived features in GPT-2 Small, but not feature spread across neurons, other LLMs, or whether the features are sparse in the model independently of the SAE representation.
Does not test completeness, stability, or canonical status of SAE features.
Does not test whether underlying features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
